prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions remain unreliable: high positive forecasts frequently overpredicted performance, while zero or negative forecasts repeatedly preceded strong wins.
Adding new screens at the finish stage (finish, new_screen) consistently hurt performance across 2 agreeing tests (-15.9% and -9.0%).
Redesigning the story stage (choose_path, redesign) was generally effective, yielding 3 winning tests (+7.6%, +5.7%, and +3.9%), though 1 test showed no clear effect.
Choose path copy updates (choose_path, copy) hurt performance in 2 agreeing tests (-3.0% and -3.7%), despite 1 winning test (+3.7%).
Adoption redesigns (adoption, redesign) and sign-in hints (sign_in, hint) produced inconsistent outcomes, driving both strong wins (+2.5% to +6.7%) and severe losses (-4.5% to -9.5%).
Finish copy updates (finish, copy) showed no clear effect across both tests (+0.9% and +1.9%), and categories with fewer than 2 agreeing tests remain thin evidence.

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] Story Screen Compact Grid Redesign: Redesign the story screen layout to a compact grid showcasing starter pet companion highlights before path choice. (why: Lessons show redesigning the story stage was effective (+7.6%, +5.7%, +3.9%). A compact layout reduces early drop-off and idling (mean 514s).)
1: [choose_path, new_flow] Story Screen Mascot Welcome Sub-Flow: Add an animated mascot greeting component and interactive sound preview to the story screen intro flow. (why: Enhances early narrative engagement at the story step where previous redesigns yielded strong gains.)
2: [adoption, redesign] Pick Friend Split View Layout: Redesign the pick friend adoption screen into a side-by-side split layout showing pet details next to selection options. (why: Adoption stage has a 21.2% drop-off rate and 89s median completion time; split layout provides clearer side-by-side companion comparison.)
3: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Status Animation & Time Info: Enable time estimates and status animation components on the waiting screen during pet rendering. (why: Home stage waiting screen takes median 201s / mean 2336s; giving clear rendering feedback keeps users engaged during background setup.)
4: [home, hint] Waiting Screen Desktop Docking Hint: Add explicit hint text explaining that your pet will dock to your desktop taskbar once setup completes. (why: Support received multiple complaints (3 emails) about pets not showing on desktop or users thinking the app won't open.)
5: [finish, hint] Home Intro System Tray Control Hint: Add hint text on home intro explaining how to reveal, move, or open controls from the system tray icon. (why: Address post-onboarding confusion (3 emails) where users are unclear how to control or unhide their pet on desktop.)
6: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Spotlight Welcome Redesign: Redesign home intro screen layout to spotlight mode with dedicated action buttons for launching pet desktop companion. (why: Finish step drop-off is high (29.6% drop) with median time 395s. A focused spotlight redesign clarifies immediate next actions.)

scores.note: choose_path redesign is a strong historical performer (+3.9% avg, 3 winning tests), though initial drop-off at this step is low.
Adding sub-flows and intro screens tends to add friction, and cost is high for interactive components.
Adoption has a 21.2% drop-off rate, but adoption redesigns have shown inconsistent historical performance (+0.8% avg).
home, wait_info has a solid track record (+2.2% across 7 tests) and directly addresses extreme home wait times via config.
Supported by 3 user email complaints, but hint changes overall carry mixed/negative historical gains.
Finish step loses 29.6% of users and has 3 support emails; cheap text update but finish hints historically show flat (+0.0%) lift.
Target step drops 29.6% of users, but finish redesigns carry high risk (-6.2% in prior tests) and require UI work.
